messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: High GPU queue growth observed for 'inference-prod' pool — autoscale not keeping up. Severity: P2. Affected: customer-facing generation endpoints. Please acknowledge with 'ack'.

maria (oncall-sre): ack. I'm looking. Can someone confirm if HPA is receiving custom metrics?

raj (ml-infra): checking prometheus -> metrics-adapter -> k8s metrics. Prometheus scrape for gpu_queue_length is spiking, adapter logs show timeouts.

lisa (eng-runtime): seeing 500ms+ tail latencies and a lot of 429 throttles on the gateway. Queue length jumped from 80 -> 180 over 8m.

alex (infra): cluster autoscaler not kicking; GPUs at 100% and nodegroups at max size. Looks like reserved capacity limits hit on a few spots.

maria (oncall-sre): summary: queues growing, HPA custom metric lagging to adapter, nodegroup scale limits reached. Customer impact: increased latency and 429s. We need triage and live mitigations.

john (support): customer reports about 5-10x latencies on chat features, some timed out requests. I have a list of affected org IDs if needed.

emma (cs): please paste org IDs, I can notify top tier customers and give ETA.

raj (ml-infra): adapter logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T12:06:01Z metrics-adapter ERROR: scrape timeout for job=inference-exporter
2026-03-15T12:06:02Z metrics-adapter WARN: failed to transform metrics -> k8s: context deadline exceeded
```

lisa (eng-runtime): prometheus shows backlog in remote_write queue too — ingestion lag ~2m. Could be CPU saturation on prom replicas.

maria (oncall-sre): immediate mitigations: 1) open temporary fallback: route non-critical models to smaller CPU-backed pool, 2) raise per-customer rate limits to reduce pressure, 3) manually scale HPA/Deployment replicas using observed kube metrics if adapter lag prevents HPA. Opinions?

alex (infra): we can spin a dedicated emergency GPU nodegroup in the same region — need approval for overcommit. If allowed, I'll start a hot-add of 4x A10s. That should absorb current backlog in ~6-8m.

raj (ml-infra): manual HPA override: `kubectl scale deploy inference-worker --replicas=30 -n prod` — I can do that but note the scheduler will fail if no nodes. Manual scale is fine once new nodes register.

maria (oncall-sre): go ahead alex, start the nodegroup. raj, prepare the `kubectl scale` command and a revert plan. lisa, start a temporary routing rule: route low-priority models to cpu-pool.

alex (infra): creating nodegroup: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed create inference-emergency --size 4 --template gpu-a10-template` — started, nodes provisioning. ETA 5-9m.

lisa (eng-runtime): routing change deployed: low-priority model traffic diverted. That immediately shaved ~20% off queue ingress.

john (support): customer list posted in thread DM, pinging top affected customers now: convo templates ready.

raj (ml-infra): adapter patch: increasing Prometheus scrape timeout and concurrency to avoid drop during spikes. Pushing a canary to metrics-adapter deployment: `kubectl set env deploy/metrics-adapter PROM_SCRAPE_TIMEOUT=15s`

maria (oncall-sre): proceed with adapter canary. We need to monitor for adapter CPU regressions.

incident-bot: UPDATE: nodegroup instances became Ready: 4 new GPU nodes registered with cluster.

raj (ml-infra): manually scaling: `kubectl scale deploy inference-worker -n prod --replicas=40` -> accepted. Pods pending scheduling for 38 -> now being placed on new nodes.

lisa (eng-runtime): within 2m after new nodes, queue drain rate increased and 429s dropped by ~70%. Latency tail improved but still elevated due to backlog.

maria (oncall-sre): mitigation status: emergency nodes added ✅, routing change ✅, manual scale ✅, adapter canary pushed ✅. Next: root cause analysis and long-term fixes: increase adapter resilience, autoscaler policies for burst, revisit nodegroup max caps, and add a fallback policy to spill to CPU pool automatically when adapter latency > threshold.

raj (ml-infra): logs show adapter errors were correlated with Prometheus remote_write backlog causing high memory/CPU. We'll look at prom replica sizing and HPA for prometheus too.

alex (infra): also found two nodegroups with conservative max sizes due to previous cost caps. I'll propose raising max for prod pools and add cost guardrails elsewhere.

emma (cs): relayed an interim message to affected customers: thanks for patience, we added capacity and are mitigating; will follow up with post-incident notes.

john (support): customers asking for ETA on full recovery — what should we tell them?

maria (oncall-sre): tell them queue backlog expected to clear in ~45-60m depending on request sizes; we will follow up with RCA and timeline for hardening.

lisa (eng-runtime): note: still seeing a small pocket of throttles from a stuck deployment (pod crashloop). Investigating if a specific image version is misbehaving — might be sticky sessions causing uneven distribution.

raj (ml-infra): follow-up actions I'm taking: 1) raise Prometheus replica CPU, 2) revert remote_write throttling changes from last week, 3) add metrics-adapter circuit-breaker + local cache to mitigate future adapter timeouts.

maria (oncall-sre): oncall handoff: I'll stay through stabilization and then hand to next oncall in 2h. Please add any follow-ups to the incident board.

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident declared P2 — create postmortem and link to #incident-management.

maria (oncall-sre): tagging next steps for RCA: timeline of events, adapter metrics, prom backlog graph, nodegroup caps, autoscaler decision logs, customer impact timeline. raj/lisa/alex please own respective sections.

emma (cs): will prepare customer communications and post-incident follow-up.

john (support): marking customers as notified. Closing customer-facing updates for now.

maria (oncall-sre): closing live mitigation — queue drain steady, no new 429s for 10m. Leaving monitoring alert to P0 if reappears. Great work team.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by maria (oncall-sre).

lisa (eng-runtime): filing a quick retrospective note in the thread: need automated fallback routing when adapter latencies exceed 2s and autoscaler fallback when nodegroup at max.

raj (ml-infra): adding tasks to infra backlog: metrics-adapter resilience, prom autoscale, more robust HPA rules with local metrics caching.

maria (oncall-sre): thanks all. I'll convert this thread into the postmortem draft after we collect graphs.
